headline.headline: MARINERS STEAL ONE IN TEN AS ALONSO WALK-OFF FALLS SHORT
headline.deck: Seattle rallies twice late to down Baltimore 6-5 in extra innings at Camden Yards
headline.body:
BALTIMORE — The Seattle Mariners needed every one of their ten innings Tuesday night, scratching out a 6-5 victory over the Baltimore Orioles before 14,728 fans at Camden Yards after a remarkable back-and-forth finish that left both dugouts spent. The Mariners, who trailed 1-0 after the first inning and did nothing at the plate through the first three frames, erupted for three runs in the fourth to seize the lead, only to watch Baltimore knot the game at five in the bottom of the ninth with a two-run rally that forced extra innings.

Seattle answered in the tenth, pushing across two runs to go ahead 6-5, and reliever Hoppe held Baltimore to just one in the bottom of the frame to earn the win. The Orioles had been hit by pitches twice during the contest, Alonso and Alexander each taking one, and Alonso's presence in the middle of the Baltimore order kept the pressure alive deep into the night. But Hoppe slammed the door, finishing off a 3:12 grind that tested every arm in both bullpens.

The victory was the kind Seattle needed to stay relevant in the American League race. Baltimore, which had clawed back twice and seemed destined for a walk-off moment in the ninth, instead fell to 5-5 in its last ten games. The Mariners board a flight home with a hard-earned road win and the knowledge that Hoppe, when the moment demanded it most, delivered.

secondary.headline: TOWNS MUST BE THE ANSWER IF KNICKS WANT TO HOLD OFF SPURS
secondary.deck: New York coach Mike Brown demands more touches for Karl-Anthony Towns as Finals open
secondary.body:
NEW YORK — The Knicks and Spurs are heading into the NBA Finals with rosters built around transcendent big men, but New York coach Mike Brown made clear Tuesday that his team cannot afford to leave Karl-Anthony Towns on the perimeter when the game is on the line. Brown called getting Towns more touches late in games an extreme priority after the Knicks offense stalled in the conference semifinals, a problem that will only become more glaring against a San Antonio front line anchored by Victor Wembanyama.

Wembanyama himself escaped a flagrant foul designation for a shove to the upper body of Knicks guard Jalen Brunson, a play that stoked tempers inside the arena and threatened to inject further physical edge into an already heated matchup. The league reviewed the incident and cleared Wembanyama without additional punishment, but the tone of the series has been set. The uniform schedules are posted, the storylines are locked in, and the question now is whether Brown can put Towns in position to punish San Antonio's defense before Wembanyama punishes New York's.

secondary.headline: HURRICANES AND GOLDEN KNIGHTS DEADLOCKED AT TWO GAMES APIECE
secondary.deck: Carolina holds off Vegas in Game 4 to even second-round series heading into pivotal Game 5
secondary.body:
RALEIGH — The Carolina Hurricanes grabbed an early lead and refused to let go Tuesday, beating the Vegas Golden Knights to square their second-round playoff series at two games each. The Hurricanes, who finished the regular season at 53-22-7 and enter the series as the superior team on paper, were pushed to the limit by a Vegas club that went 39-26-17 in the Pacific Division and has made a habit of postseason trouble-making.

Game 4 takeaways center on Carolina's ability to control pace when ahead, and on Vegas's tendency to apply relentless pressure in the late periods. With the series even and a fifth game looming, the next two weeks could define both franchises. Carolina is the deeper team, but the Golden Knights have shown they can manufacture offense against anyone. This series is far from over.

secondary.headline: DODGERS POUND PIRATES 12-3 AS PAGES LAUNCHES NUMBER 15
secondary.deck: Los Angeles pours on ten runs in the seventh inning to bury Pittsburgh and end four-game skid
secondary.body:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Pirates entered Tuesday hoping to snap a four-game losing streak in front of their home fans. Instead they were steamrolled by the Los Angeles Dodgers, who scored ten runs in a single seventh inning to turn a close game into a 12-3 rout before 30,646 at PNC Park. Pittsburgh had jumped ahead 2-0 in the first inning on a Bryan Reynolds home run, his seventh of the season, but the Dodgers chipped away and then detonated in the seventh in one of the most lopsided single-inning performances of the early summer.

Andy Pages led the Los Angeles charge with his 15th home run of the season, and Ryan O'Hearn added his tenth. Shohei Ohtani doubled and was lifted for a pinch hitter in the eighth, a sign that the Dodgers were managing his workload in a blowout. Los Angeles, now 43-24 and sitting first in the NL West, has built a commanding lead in the division. The Pirates fall to 34-33, their playoff hopes requiring an immediate turnaround that Tuesday night's performance did nothing to inspire.

column.headline: THE KNICKS WILL LIVE OR DIE BY TOWNS IN THESE FINALS
column.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns was brought to New York for exactly this moment. A seven-foot center with a shooting range that extends well beyond the three-point line, Towns is the one Knick who can look Victor Wembanyama in the eye and score on him in the post, at the elbow, or from the arc. Mike Brown knows it. Every scout in the league knows it. The only question left is whether the Knicks will actually feed him the ball when the fourth quarter gets tight and the crowd gets loud and the easy shot turns into a contested one. History suggests they will retreat to isolation ball. History needs to be wrong this time.

The Wembanyama shove on Brunson and the league's decision to let it go without a flagrant ruling sends a signal that the officials will allow this series to be physical. That suits San Antonio, which has the size and length to bother every New York ball-handler. The Knicks counter with Towns, or they do not counter at all. Brown had better not wait until the series is in trouble to make that adjustment. These Finals will be decided in the paint, and Towns has spent his entire career preparing for a stage this big.

story.headline: MARINERS SURVIVE ORIOLES IN TEN, DODGERS EXPLODE FOR SEVEN IN SEVENTH
story.deck: Seattle rallies past Baltimore in extras while Los Angeles crushes Pittsburgh with stunning frame
story.body:
BALTIMORE, Md. -- The Seattle Mariners scratched out two runs in the tenth inning Tuesday night to beat the Baltimore Orioles 6-5 at Camden Yards, escaping a game that saw the Orioles load the bases to the tune of 23 men left on base and twice force Seattle's hand in extra frames. Randy Arozarena clubbed his seventh homer of the season and Mitch Garver added his third as the Mariners staged a four-run fourth inning to seize control, only to watch Baltimore's Coby Mayo blast his ninth home run in the ninth to knot the game at five and send it to extras. Hoppe earned the win in relief as Seattle pushed across the decisive runs in the tenth against an Orioles bullpen that simply ran out of answers.

In Pittsburgh, the Los Angeles Dodgers turned an otherwise dormant afternoon into a rout by sending 13 batters to the plate in a ten-run seventh inning that turned a 2-2 tie into a laugher, with the Dodgers ultimately winning 12-3 before 30,646 at PNC Park. Andy Pages reached double-digit home run territory with his 15th blast of the year, while Bryan Reynolds slugged his seventh for the Pirates in a losing effort. Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman each notched doubles in the Dodger barrage, which pushed Los Angeles to 43-24 and extended Pittsburgh's losing skid to five straight games.

Elsewhere around the majors, the St. Louis Cardinals blanked the New York Mets 7-0 at Citi Field behind Alec Burleson's ninth homer and a stingy pitching performance that held New York scoreless across all nine innings, stretching the Cardinals' winning streak to six games. The Detroit Tigers pounded out a 10-4 victory over the Minnesota Twins despite a one-hour-51-minute rain delay, with Dillon Dingler belting his 16th home run and seven players combining for the long ball across a game that saw four hit batters. The New York Yankees edged the Cleveland Guardians 3-2, with a solo shot by Jones in the first at-bat credited to him providing crucial insurance in a taut pitchers' duel at Progressive Field.

story.headline: WEMBANYAMA CLEARED, BUT TENSIONS BOIL OVER INSIDE ARENA AND OUT AS FINALS HEAT UP
story.deck: Spurs star avoids flagrant ruling while chaos erupts at Manhattan watch party
story.body:
Victor Wembanyama will not face a flagrant foul penalty for shoving Jalen Brunson in the upper body during Game 3 of the NBA Finals, the league announced Wednesday, sparing San Antonio's franchise cornerstone from automatic suspension concerns heading into a series that grows more combustible by the hour. The 22-year-old Frenchman, who has averaged 31 points and nine blocks through the first three games, addressed the ruling with characteristic directness, telling reporters he had no intention of injuring Brunson but refusing to apologize for the physicality. Brunson, nursing a sore shoulder, practiced fully Wednesday and declared himself ready.

Off the court, Wembanyama took a separate and solemn moment to condemn acts of violence targeting Spurs fans in New York, after multiple incidents were reported in and around Madison Square Garden during the series. His statement, released through the Spurs organization, called the behavior 'unacceptable and shameful' and urged fans of both franchises to 'let basketball be the only battle.' The plea came as New York City police confirmed eight arrests following a watch party in Manhattan on Monday night that organizers billed as a family-friendly gathering but that authorities described as having turned 'incredibly reckless,' with altercations breaking out among hundreds of attendees near Times Square.

On the strategic front, Knicks assistant Mike Brown stressed Tuesday that getting Karl-Anthony Towns more touches in the fourth quarter is 'extremely important' after New York's half-court offense stalled badly in Game 3's final six minutes, producing just four points. Towns, who scored 28 in the first half of that contest, touched the ball only twice after the four-minute mark as the Spurs' length smothered New York's perimeter options. Adding another layer of intrigue, both franchises released their uniform schedules for the remainder of the Finals, with the Knicks set to wear their classic orange threads for Game 4 on Thursday night at MSG, a look in which New York is 7-2 this postseason.

story.headline: STAAL BELLY GOAL SQUARES STANLEY CUP FINAL AT 2-2
story.deck: Carolina captain scores twice, including stomach-down third-period winner to stun Vegas.
story.body:
Jordan Staal scored one of the most improbable goals of this Stanley Cup Final, sliding across the ice on his stomach and still finding the net at 6:32 of the third period, lifting the Carolina Hurricanes to a 5-3 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights in Game 4 on Tuesday night and evening the series at two games apiece.

Staal's second goal of the game proved to be the dagger after Carolina built an early lead and spent much of the evening fending off a Vegas squad that refused to fold. The Golden Knights, 39-26-17 on the season out of the Pacific Division, made enough noise to keep the sellout crowd nervous, but the Hurricanes' 53-22-7 regular-season dominance showed through when it mattered most in the third period.

With the series now knotted at 2-2, Game 5 looms as a true turning point. Staal addressed the mental demands facing both clubs, noting that resilience and focus separate teams at this stage of the postseason. Carolina will look to reclaim home-ice advantage when the two clubs meet again later this week.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS RETOOL FOR 2026 SEASON
story.deck: Several franchises made bold moves this spring to reshape their rosters at the most important position.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-blown quarterback market this May, with the Las Vegas Raiders leading the charge by agreeing to a three-year, $132 million deal with veteran signal-caller Sam Darnold, who parlayed a strong 2025 campaign in Minnesota into the richest contract of his career. The Cleveland Browns, still searching for stability under center, swung a second-round pick to the New England Patriots for backup Drake Maye insurance, while the New Orleans Saints quietly restructured Derek Carr's remaining contract to clear cap space for additional offensive weapons heading into training camp.

The 2026 NFL Draft in late April delivered its share of surprises, most notably when the Tennessee Titans selected Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders with the fourth overall pick after trading up from ninth, sending shockwaves through draft boards across the league. The Jacksonville Jaguars, picking second, took Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith to pair with Trevor Lawrence, a move that drew widespread praise from analysts who called it the steal of the entire draft. Several teams that passed on premium skill positions in the first round moved aggressively in free agency to compensate.

As rosters take shape ahead of July training camps, the defending Super Bowl LX champion Philadelphia Eagles remain the team to beat in the NFC, with general manager Howie Roseman having re-signed cornerstone linebacker Nakobe Dean to a four-year extension worth $68 million. The Kansas City Chiefs, stung by their February loss in New Orleans, have retooled their secondary by signing cornerback Sauce Gardner away from the New York Jets in a stunning free agency coup, while head coach Andy Reid confirmed the team expects Patrick Mahomes to be fully healthy after offseason knee maintenance that kept him limited through March.
